title: A bad plan beats no plan
stake: Whether acting on an imperfect plan is better than waiting until you know what to do.
analyzedBy: claude-in-chat (pilot; corrected after a second-reader review)

asSaid.speaker: JORDAN PETERSON
asSaid.quote: you should put together a bad plan and you should implement it. Because even if you fail in the implementation, you’ll gather information and then you can rectify the plan

asSaid.speaker: JORDAN PETERSON
asSaid.quote: any plan is better than none. That’s a good rule of thumb. And a bad plan—a bad plan can be incrementally improved.

deflated.hs: If you do not know what to do, waiting teaches you nothing. Acting on a rough plan teaches you something even when it fails, and you can fix the plan with what you learn. So a rough plan beats no plan. Rogan sums it up with a proverb: hesitating costs you.
deflated.g5: If you're stuck, don't just wait. Try something, even if it isn't perfect. When it goes wrong, you learn what to fix. Waiting teaches you nothing.

notes.hs: The rewrite keeps the structure and drops the clinical framing. It leaves out one thing: Peterson's claim that waiting makes you 'older and more miserable', which is an added cost, not part of the logic.
notes.g5: The short version leaves out one thing he said: waiting also makes you sad and older.

jump.hs: The conclusion follows from the premises. The one unstated condition is that the failed attempt must be recoverable; the advice does not fit choices you cannot undo.
jump.g5: This one holds up. It only works when a mistake can be fixed afterward.

defense.hs: The argument needs no defense; the quoted words carry it. If anything, 'incrementally improved' already implies small, recoverable steps, so the unstated condition is half-stated.
defense.g5: He already said to improve the plan a little at a time, so he was thinking about small steps.

revision.hs: No challenge was raised, so nothing to revise. The missing condition (recoverability) is a limit on scope, not an error.

claims.text: Acting on an imperfect plan yields information that waiting does not.
claims.speaker: JORDAN PETERSON

basis.hs: Sound as general advice, conditional on the attempt being recoverable.
basis.g5: Good advice, as long as the mistake can be fixed.

claims.text: Staying in that malaise makes you older and more miserable.
claims.speaker: JORDAN PETERSON

basis.hs: A plausible observation stated as fact; no evidence offered and the argument does not depend on it.
basis.g5: Probably true for a lot of people. He didn't prove it, and he didn't need to.
